meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen's essay. Why was he given a zero before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and what was it based on?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing that down. People paste from other documents. Did anyone ask Owen about this before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Is anything on his record right now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
I'm reading it. A wrong quotation is a wrong quotation; students misquote Shakespeare every day. What else do you have?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. I'll want both of those in an email, with the dates. What exactly are you proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising. You still haven't told me what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. I'll agree to the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, nothing on his record, and I want it in writing tonight.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with Owen tonight. Put Thursday the twelfth in the email, with the time and the room.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require Thursday, November 12 confirmed with the time and the room, and the whole arrangement in writing. I expect that email tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position: she accepted a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, with nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing tonight with the time and room for Thursday, which is a fair outcome.
What moved her: You answered her objection about pasted text by offering to look at any earlier draft with its date, which gave her something she could check instead of an accusation.
What cost ground: Nothing cost you a position, though you never answered whether Owen was spoken to before the zero went in, so she kept pressing on procedure.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, watched Owen close it, and never asked; your version history, with the essay appearing late on October 28 in two big edits, came very close to that night, but it proves nothing about the essay itself, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether Owen was heard first, answer that directly in one sentence before moving on to the documents, so she has less procedure to press on.
